title: Document one thing you learned from another discipline
why_matters: What you learned from shadowing only matters if it changes how you work. Writing it down — and sharing it back — turns a private observation into a team artefact. The smallest version of this is one paragraph; that's all you need. The act of writing it back to the team is what creates the credit.
steps: Look at your shadowing notes. Pick one observation that has a clear behaviour you could adopt.
Write a short paragraph: what you observed, why it matters, what you're going to do differently. Three to five sentences total.
Send it to the person you shadowed first; ask if it's a fair read.
Adjust based on their feedback, then file it under "Probation evidence — what I learned from other disciplines".
success_criteria: A short paragraph exists in your evidence file. The person you shadowed has reviewed and acknowledged. The behaviour change is specific and testable.
reflection_prompt: What's the version of this you weren't ready to write — and what would have to be true for you to write it next month?
